analyst_view.overall: Liverpool (5th, 18 points) host Manchester United (19th, 8 points, their worst Premier League start) in the derby, in Mauricio Pochettino's first game after replacing Michael Carrick during the international break. Match-day previews (The Independent via LiveScore, Khel Now) expect him to keep Carrick's 4-2-3-1 with a mid-block, Tielemans and Mainoo shielding the defence and Mbeumo leading the line in place of the injured Sesko, with a back three the alternative. Liverpool have struggled at Anfield (four league goals in their first five home games), but van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong are available; Ekitike (counted), Bradley and Leoni are out. United are without Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte (all counted), and Rashford and Luke Shaw (both rarely used, leaving Amass as the only specialist left-back); Lisandro Martinez is back from his ban. The derby boost to cards (about +39%) and referee Sam Barrott (4.1 cards a game, close to average) are already in the numbers; I could not find the confirmed XIs before writing, so the view rests on the match-day predicted sides.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already adding about 4% to Liverpool for United's leaky defence (16 conceded in six) and taking Sesko off United. Liverpool scored only four goals in their first five home league games, and Pochettino, with a few sessions, is expected to start compact with Tielemans and Mainoo screening and Mbeumo as a makeshift striker, so I lean slightly lower: about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, already trimming a little for Liverpool conceding few corners lately. United, in the bottom three, are expected to keep the gaps small and defend deeper at Anfield in Pochettino's first game, while Liverpool should push down the flanks with Frimpong available again; I lean mildly higher, about 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already adding about 39% for the derby, a little for Sam Barrott (4.1 a game in 54 games) and for United's high recent card count (16 in six). Mac Allister is one booking from a ban, and a United side defending deep may still commit tactical fouls, but the derby boost is already large, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, already adding about 11% to United for their busy attacking under Carrick (96 shots in six). Away at Anfield, without their striker Sesko, and with a new manager focused first on midfield stability and keeping the team compact, United are likely to take fewer attempts than that, which outweighs Liverpool's near-full attack: about 30.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, already adding about 7% to Liverpool for United conceding plenty on target lately. Fewer United attempts and Liverpool's weak home finishing this season pull down, while a mostly fit Liverpool attack with Isak and Wirtz, plus United's leaky defence (19 league goals conceded), pull up, so I stay at 9.8.
